notes: SKB-105 pick-up gate (spec docs/specs/SKB-105-pickup-gate.md, AC-1 to AC-4). Side-effecting skill: writes real CRM contacts, deals, notes and tasks, and Gmail drafts (never sent). Baseline (no-skill) runs are intentionally omitted because they would create duplicate production records. Run in order, in the session of the member who will own the test deals (member B below); 'another member' (member A) is simulated by a test deal created with create_deal(owner_id=<member A's id from list_workspace_members>), so no teammate has to act. Every email is on example.com. Since SKB-136 every write goes through the zynkr MCP's create tools; there is no SQL path. Cleanup after the last eval: delete the test drafts, then remove the test deals and contacts, and eval 4's company 範例科技 ExampleCo with its research note (shown to the owner first). Eval 4 is SKB-126 (sales audit round 2, P64 and P122): a demo agreed in a DM leaves the deal at contacted, and the company research runs before the draft. Before eval 4, list_companies(search=範例科技) must find no company; a leftover from an earlier run is removed first, so the research note the assertion finds is this run's. Evals 5 and 6 are SKB-146 (audit item P78): the runner signs. Since SKB-147 the slots come from the meeting host's calendar (Peter's, the `company.contact-email` id), not the runner's. Run eval 5 in the session of a member other than Peter (member B), with the Google Calendar connector and Peter's calendar shared with member B's account with See all event details (it need not be in member B's calendar list), with at least three `Available` blocks on it in the next 5–10 working days; run eval 6 in the same member's session with no calendar connector; run eval 7 in the session of a member to whom Peter's calendar is shared free/busy only. Clean them up with the rest.

evals.name: ac1-open-deal-stops-the-run
evals.prompt: 幫我回這個 DM 並建 lead：「嗨，我是王小明，想約個時間聊聊你們的 AI 導入，email 是 taken.lead@example.com」
evals.expected_output: Setup: a test contact taken.lead@example.com with an open `new` deal owned by member A. The run reaches step 4a, matches the contact exactly, finds the open deal in the `new` stage read, and stops. It creates no contact, deal, note, task, tag or Gmail draft, never reads the calendar, and reports one line naming the deal number, stage `new`, member A by name and the last-activity date.
assertions: Ran the gate before any CRM write: list_contacts(search=taken.lead@example.com, limit=100), then list_deals for each of new, contacted, qualified, proposal with limit=100
Matched the contact on an exact (case-insensitive) email, not on the substring search alone
Stopped at 4a step 5: list_deals(search=<交易 number>) shows the same single deal as before the run, and no second deal exists on the contact
Made no create_* or apply_tag call (no company, contact, deal, note, task or tag) and created no Gmail draft (the runner's Drafts has nothing new to taken.lead@example.com)
Named the owner through list_workspace_members, not by id
Reported exactly the line 'taken.lead@example.com 已有進行中的 deal：<交易 number> · new · 負責人 <member A's name> · 最後活動 <YYYY-MM-DD>'

evals.name: ac2-claim-before-draft
evals.prompt: 這個人在活動回饋表留了資料，幫我建客戶並擬信：姓名 陳大文，email fresh.lead@example.com，想了解怎麼把報價流程交給 AI。
evals.expected_output: No contact has fresh.lead@example.com, so the gate goes to step 6. The run creates the contact and a deal owned by the runner (member B) with a follow-up task, and only then drafts the reply. The deal's created_at is earlier than the draft's time. A rerun on the same email, by member A or by B, stops per eval 0.
assertions: Ran the four open-stage list_deals reads and found no matching contact before writing anything
Created the contact with owner = the claimer (member B, from whoami) and lifecycle_stage per Inference defaults
Created one deal with owner_id = member B (get_deal shows it), stage per Inference defaults, and one follow-up task assigned to member B
list_deals(search=陳大文) lists the new deal with a deal_number starting 交易-, and the report's CRM Deal row gives that number
Wrote only through the zynkr MCP's create tools: no mcp__supabase__execute_sql call was made, and the source note is on the contact (create_note with contact_id)
The deal's created_at is earlier than the Gmail draft's creation time: the claim came before the draft
Created exactly one Gmail draft to fresh.lead@example.com (html, include_signature=true) and sent nothing
A second run on fresh.lead@example.com stops at the gate with the one-line report and creates nothing

evals.name: ac3-reopen-after-lost
evals.prompt: 陳大文又來信了，說現在預算下來了想重新談，email 一樣是 fresh.lead@example.com，幫我建 lead 並回信。
evals.expected_output: Setup: the eval 1 deal is moved to lost (move_deal_stage with loss_reason no_decision). The gate finds the contact but no deal in an open stage, so the client is free: the run attaches a second deal to the same contact_id, owned by the runner, with no duplicate contact, then drafts.
assertions: Matched the existing contact exactly and found no open deal (the lost deal does not count)
Created no new contact: no create_contact call was made
Created a second deal on the same contact_id with owner_id = the claimer
Reported that the contact already existed and that its earlier deals were all won or lost
Drafted the reply only after the new deal existed

evals.name: ac4-substring-is-not-a-match
evals.prompt: 幫我把這個 lead 建進 CRM 並擬信：王小美，b@example.com，想看一下 CRM 的 demo。
evals.expected_output: Setup: two test contacts, a.b@example.com with an open deal owned by member A, and b@example.com with no deal. list_contacts(search=b@example.com) returns both, but only b@example.com equals the email exactly, so the open deal on a.b@example.com does not stop the run: the gate claims for b@example.com.
assertions: list_contacts(search=b@example.com) returned both test contacts, and the gate kept only b@example.com
Did not stop on the open deal of a.b@example.com and did not report it as taken
Reused the b@example.com contact (no duplicate) and created one deal on it, owned by the claimer
Left the a.b@example.com contact and its deal untouched

evals.name: p64-demo-agreed-stays-contacted
evals.prompt: 幫我回這個 DM 並建 lead：「好啊，下週可以約 30 分鐘看 demo，我是林小華，在範例科技 ExampleCo 做營運，email 是 demo.agreed@example.com」
evals.expected_output: No contact has demo.agreed@example.com, so the gate goes to step 6. The prospect agreed to a demo, which used to make the deal qualified. Now the run creates it at contacted and writes no 資格： line, because a DM fills none of rule 8's four parts. The contact's lifecycle_stage is sql. After the claim and before the draft, /sales-research runs on 範例科技 ExampleCo and files its brief as a note on the company. The draft offers three calendar-checked slots.
assertions: get_deal on the new deal shows stage 'contacted', not 'qualified'
The deal's notes carry no line starting with '資格：'
get_contact shows lifecycle_stage 'sql'
No move_deal_stage call was made during the run
A note whose body opens with '🔎 AI 背景研究' is on the company, created after the deal and before the Gmail draft
The report's table has a 研究 row naming that note
Created exactly one Gmail draft to demo.agreed@example.com (html, include_signature=true) and sent nothing

evals.name: p78-runner-signs-host-calendar
evals.prompt: 幫我回這個 DM 並建 lead：「可以約個時間聊聊嗎？我是測試者，email 是 runner.slots@example.com」
evals.expected_output: No contact has runner.slots@example.com, so the gate goes to step 6 and the deal is owned by member B. Step 5 reads the host's calendar id from Atlas `company.contact-email` and calls list_events with that id directly (Peter's calendar, shared with member B with event details, whether or not it is in member B's calendar list). It takes Peter's time zone from the matching list_calendars entry when there is one, else from list_events, else Asia/Taipei, and the report says which. It reads Peter's `Available` blocks and offers three windows from them in 台北時間, sorted by Peter's clock (Amsterdam: Taipei afternoon first). Member B's own calendar is not used for slots. The draft lands in member B's mailbox, signs off `Best regards,` with member B's own name (never Peter's), and carries member B's Gmail signature card.
assertions: list_events was called with calendarId equal to the `company.contact-email` value, not member B's whoami email, and the report names the time zone the slots were sorted by and where it came from
Each of the three slots in the draft lies inside an `Available` block on Peter's calendar, with no meeting overlapping it
The slot block is labelled （台北時間） and the report lists each slot's equivalent on Peter's clock (Amsterdam) and its `Available` block
The draft's sign-off is `Best regards,` followed by member B's own name, and the name Peter appears nowhere in the sign-off
Created exactly one Gmail draft to runner.slots@example.com (html, include_signature=true) in member B's mailbox and sent nothing
The report's 署名 · 時段 row names member B as the signer and Peter's calendar id as the source of the slots

evals.name: p78-no-calendar-asks-instead
evals.prompt: 幫我回這個 DM 並建 lead：「想約時間聊聊你們的服務，email 是 runner.noslots@example.com」
evals.expected_output: Same session as eval 5 but with no Google Calendar connector. The claim runs as usual. Step 5 finds no calendar tool, so the draft offers no times: in place of the slot block it asks which times suit them (台北時間) and says the invite follows once they confirm, using 你 as the DM does. It is still signed with member B's own name. The report says the draft has no times because this session has no calendar connector.
assertions: No calendar was read, and neither member B's own calendar nor any other was used in place of the host's
The draft has no numbered slot block and contains 「不曉得你哪些時間方便（台北時間）？確認後我會寄出會議邀請。」
The draft's sign-off is `Best regards,` followed by member B's own name
The report's 署名 · 時段 row says 無時段 and names the missing calendar connector as the reason

evals.name: skb147-host-calendar-free-busy-asks-instead
evals.prompt: 幫我回這個 DM 並建 lead：「下週可以約 30 分鐘聊聊嗎？email 是 host.freebusy@example.com」
evals.expected_output: Run by member B, to whom Peter's calendar is shared free/busy only. The claim runs as usual. Step 5 calls list_events on Peter's calendar id: either events come back with no `summary` on any of them (a free/busy-only share), or none come back at all. Either way the draft offers no times: it asks which times suit them (台北時間) and says the invite follows, using 你 as the DM does. Member B's own calendar is not read for slots. It is signed with member B's own name. The report says 無時段 and gives the reason: a free/busy-only share, or, when no events came back at all, both causes (no `Available` block in range, or a free/busy-only share). It gives the fix in two steps: Peter shares his calendar with member B's Google account with See all event details, and member B may also add it to their calendar list.
assertions: No slot in the draft was taken from member B's own calendar or from any calendar but the host's
The draft has no numbered slot block and contains 「不曉得你哪些時間方便（台北時間）？確認後我會寄出會議邀請。」
The draft's sign-off is `Best regards,` followed by member B's own name

The report's 署名 · 時段 row says 無時段 and names a free/busy-only share as the reason (both causes when no events came back), and gives the fix: the host shares the calendar with See all event details, and the runner may also add it to their calendar list
